reason: The after-meal picture shows glucose beside insulin-producing cells, so I’ll start with that signal.
expectation: The meal glucose should prompt the pancreatic cells to release insulin.

effect: Glucose combined automatically with liver cells, completing liver storage instead of releasing insulin. I still need to trigger the pancreatic signal.
reaction: I was surprised the glucose itself did not work at the pancreatic cells.
reason: The pancreatic picture shows glucose in the adjacent blood, so I’ll try the blood at those cells.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will release insulin into the blood.

effect: Blood at the pancreatic cells produced insulin in blood, so I can now try the muscle-storage step.
reaction: The blood pairing makes sense now that the insulin is shown entering the vessel.
reason: The muscle picture shows receptors for blood-carried insulin and glucose already nearby.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin should help the muscle take in and store glucose.

effect: Insulin helped muscle store glucose, completing that goal; the remaining goal concerns the liver between meals.
reaction: It was useful to see that insulin is a message rather than part of the stored carbohydrate.
reason: The between-meal pancreatic cells contain glucagon, and blood carried the insulin message in the earlier step.
expectation: The cells should release glucagon into the blood, making the liver-release message available.

effect: Glucagon is now in the blood and available to signal the liver to release glucose.
reaction: The parallel with insulin makes the two messages easier to follow.
reason: The picture and goal connect glucagon to the liver's stored carbohydrate.
expectation: The glucagon message should prompt the liver to break down its store and release glucose.

effect: Glucagon prompted the liver store to release glucose into the blood, completing the between-meal goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the stored glucose become available again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using insulin to store glucose in muscle was worthwhile because it showed the difference between a message and the material being stored.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first attempt was confusing: glucose appeared beside the pancreatic cells, but combining it with them instead triggered liver storage.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the glucose-and-pancreas attempt automatically combined glucose with the liver instead.

arbitrary.text: Using blood rather than meal glucose to trigger insulin was not obvious at first, though the result showed insulin entering the blood.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: comparing insulin and glucagon made the connection between meals and stored fuel understandable.
